title: Dave's reasons for leaving the road and the final concert, then Gerry Mulligan
summary: Dave wanted time with his kids and finances allowed it; after the last concert George Wein got him together with Gerry Mulligan, Alan Dawson and Jack Six.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And he wanted to spend more time, you know, with his kids and all that.
I wondered if he was conflicted about missing baseball games and missing birthdays?

Yeah all that kind of stuff, yeah. And actually our second oldest brother had a lot of issues that, you know, he wasn’t around to deal with and I think he had a lot of sort of guilt around that. So I think that was a big part of it too, wanting to be able to help him.

But it’s also interesting to note, and if I have my history right, that after he broke up the group and their last concert was in Pittsburgh, and I remember being impressed seeing John Chancellor from the NBC Nightly News, that was the button on the national newscast, the Dave Brubeck Quartet gave their last concert tonight. You know it’s still of that much importance. And I think that coming summer George Wein said, “You know © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Dave, you’ve never really played with Gerry” — Gerry Mulligan. He lives in Greenwich just down the road. You guys would probably be a potent force you know, if you — and so you know after not being on the road for six months maybe Dave missed it a little more than he thought he would.
Yeah, or maybe he thought, you know with the quartet it was just a constant grind, but that he could pick and choose. Some concerts but —
Everyone’s an independent contractor and no one’s on salary and you know there’s a different sense of obligation.
If George Wein puts it together and pays Gerry and pays him.
Right. And you know Alan Dawson was a brilliant drummer and Jack Six and those guys made some wonderful records together.
So he sort of had his cake and ate it too. He was liberated from doing 150 concerts a year, but he could still play jazz with Gerry and Alan and Jack.
